subject: Geography
description: Himalayas, Aravallis, Vindhyas, Western/Eastern Ghats, Satpura

questions.stem: The highest peak lying entirely within India is:
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) — third-highest in the world — lies on the India-Nepal border with its main peak in Sikkim. Everest (8,849 m) straddles Nepal-China, not Indian territory. K2 (8,611 m) lies in the Pakistan-administered part of Kashmir. Nanda Devi (7,816 m in Uttarakhand) is the highest peak entirely within undisputed Indian territory.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Aravalli range, one of the oldest fold mountains in the world, runs through which state?
questions.explanation: The Aravallis run ~670 km mainly through Rajasthan (from Palanpur in Gujarat to Delhi, via Udaipur, Ajmer, Alwar). Highest peak: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu. These are among the world's oldest mountains (Proterozoic age, ~350 million years older than the Himalayas), heavily eroded today. They separate the Thar desert from the Ganga plain.

questions.stem: The highest peak in the Western Ghats (and of peninsular India) is:
questions.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala's Eravikulam National Park is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India. Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest in the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu). Mahendragiri (1,501 m) lies in the Eastern Ghats of Odisha. 'Vindhyachal' is another name for the Vindhya range, not a single peak.

questions.stem: Match the mountain range with the state it chiefly runs through. A. Satpura. B. Vindhya. C. Zaskar. D. Karakoram. List-II: 1. Madhya Pradesh, 2. MP/Uttar Pradesh border, 3. Ladakh (J&K), 4. Ladakh (disputed PoK).
questions.explanation: Satpura — Madhya Pradesh; separates the Narmada and Tapi rivers. Vindhya — Madhya Pradesh/UP border; separates northern and peninsular India. Zaskar — an eastern Himalayan range largely within Ladakh. Karakoram — contains K2 and several 8,000-m peaks; parts pass through Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK) and Aksai Chin (disputed with China).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Himalayan range divides into three parallel mountain belts. The northernmost and highest belt is called the:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas have three longitudinal belts — from north to south: Himadri (Great Himalayas) with the highest peaks (Everest, Kanchenjunga), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) in the middle with hill stations like Shimla and Darjeeling, and Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas) — youngest, lowest. Purvanchal is the eastern offshoot running into NE India (Patkai, Naga, Mizo and Manipur hills).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at the:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats converge in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu. The Palghat Gap (Palakkad) is a pass through the Western Ghats that connects Kerala and Tamil Nadu, not a meeting point of the two Ghats. Cardamom Hills lie further south in the Western Ghats. Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is the famous hill station in the Nilgiris.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Mount K2, the second-highest peak in the world, lies in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) — after Everest (8,849 m) the second-highest peak — lies in the Karakoram range, on the China-Pakistan border within the disputed region of Gilgit-Baltistan (which India claims as part of J&K). Four of the world's 14 'eight-thousanders' are in the Karakoram. Hindu Kush lies chiefly in Afghanistan; Pamirs straddle Tajikistan, Afghanistan and China.
